memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: When you lay siege to a city for a long time, fighting against it to capture it, do not destroy its trees by putting an ax to them, because you can eat their fruit. Do not cut them down. Are the trees of the field people, that you should besiege them? - Deut 20:19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
In the middle of laws about warfare, God gives a striking command, do not needlessly destroy the fruit trees around a besieged city. Even in war, there were limits. The fruit trees provided food and were not the enemy. God asks a gentle, almost poetic question, "Are the trees of the field people, that you should besiege them?" Destroying them would be senseless waste.

This is remarkable. Even in the harsh reality of war, God calls His people to restraint and care for creation. He did not permit reckless destruction of what sustains life. There is wisdom and mercy here that goes beyond the battle, God cares about how His people treat the world He made, even in difficult times.

This reflects God's character as a good Creator who values His creation and calls us to be responsible stewards of it. From the beginning, humanity was entrusted with caring for the earth, not destroying it carelessly (Gen 2:15). We honour God when we treat His creation with respect rather than reckless waste. This principle touches how we use resources, care for our environment, and avoid needless destruction. God's concern extends even to trees, a reminder that nothing He has made is treated as worthless. How might God be calling you to be a more careful, grateful steward of the world He has given?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How do you treat the created world God has given?
2. Where might you avoid needless waste?
3. What does grateful stewardship look like in your daily life?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for the world You made and entrusted to us. Help me be a careful, grateful steward of Your good creation. Amen.
